<!--
Shared chart color palette, spliced into every report page via
{{< include _chart_theme.qmd >}} (same literal-text-splice mechanism as
_calib_run_selector.qmd -- these cells execute in the including page's own
OJS runtime, not a separate document). Pure OJS, no Python dependency, so
include order relative to _calib_run_selector.qmd doesn't matter.

Replaces the old, inconsistent per-page defaults (navy/olive #376092 /
#77933c on most pages, "steelblue"/"forestgreen"/"orange" on others) with
one palette used everywhere -- drawn from the WFRC brand extension's
documented swatches (_extensions/WFRCAnalytics/wfrc-brand/assets/theme/
_wfrc-colors.scss) rather than invented tones, and validated against the
dataviz skill's categorical checks (Model/Target/TargetAlt/Accent clear
lightness, chroma, and CVD-separation on the site's light surface #fcfcfb;
Model's contrast WARN at 2.79:1 needs relief via direct labels/legend,
not a bare fill). Meaning stays consistent site-wide:

  themeModel        Modeled data, always
  themeTarget       Target/comparison-baseline data (primary source, e.g.
                     survey, count, or calibration target)
  themeTargetAlt    A second, distinct target source in the same chart
                     (e.g. an older survey year shown alongside a newer one)
  themeTargetLight  Faded/secondary variant of Target (e.g. a
                     distribution band behind a Target mean marker)
  themeAccent       Extra category beyond Model/Target (e.g. a
                     calibration target line)
  themeNeutral      Neutral/reference series, not itself Model or Target
  themeDanger       Over-threshold / error highlight
-->

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
themeModel = "#ea7b00"       // WFRC core orange
themeTarget = "#036fa8"      // WFRC core blue
themeTargetAlt = "#007426"   // WFRC core green
themeTargetLight = "#8ebed8" // Lighter tint of Target blue (#036fa8)
themeAccent = "#9d4879"      // WFRC RTP fuschia
themeNeutral = "#7f7a76"     // WFRC brand gray
themeDanger = "#d32f00"      // WFRC core red -- status color, pair with a label/icon, never color alone
```
